asr_text: You go to buy your usual coffee, then stop. Hey, when did you go upscale? The first thing that comes to mind is tariffs. You wanna say, so you're the culprit? But a great detective takes a breath here. Let's turn back the clock on this case. In the United States, the average price of ground coffee rose 41% from the same month a year earlier, according to reports based on government figures. This is about ground coffee, not a cup at a cafe. Before you buy something to wake you up, the price shocks your wallet awake. But according to Reuters, most of the rise in store prices came from bean shortages that began before the summer tariffs, and from higher prices for the beans themselves. Wait a minute, the case had started before the suspect we had our eye on even appeared.
